source.title: Probing Layer-wise Memorization and Generalization in Deep Neural Networks via Model Stitching
source.authors: Aishwarya Gupta; Indranil Saha; Piyush Rai

record.tranche_reason: Uses model stitching to test how replacing model layers changes memorization and test accuracy; it does not directly test the listed architecture, optimizer, batch-size, regularization, width, sharpness, or example-removal versions.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates partially noisy-label training, stitched-model accuracy on randomly labeled training inputs, and accuracy on clean held-out test data. None of the listed versions covers these layer-stitching interventions. Results cited from prior work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures where deliberately induced label-noise memorization resides and how stitching or fine-tuning changes it. It does not test V1's comparison of natural-label learning with fully random-label learning, or any intervention or comparison named by V2–V8. Its layer-level findings fit none of the supplied versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that early layers contribute to noise memorization and that replacing them can suppress random-label recall and improve test accuracy; clean heads prevent perfect memorization in their stitched models. Critical depths vary with architecture and dataset. Noise propagation and amplification are proposed explanations, rather than independently established mechanisms.
record.recipe_differences: Compares clean and partially noisy models through post-training layer stitching, rather than testing the listed claim conditions; it also fine-tunes individual layers in an appendix.
record.method_sensitivity: Stitching depth, stitching direction, architecture, dataset complexity, and noise ratio change the reported outcomes. ViT results include deviations and fluctuations.

fits_no_version.finding: Replacing noisy prefixes with clean prefixes suppresses random-label recall and restores clean-test accuracy; reversing the stitching direction produces depth-dependent memorization without full random-label recall.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Functional contributions to noise memorization and generalization depend on stitching direction, depth, architecture, and dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning individual blocks can correct labels on previously corrupted inputs, with test-accuracy effects depending on noise level; selected clean middle-block insertions suppress memorization without recovering clean-model test accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Layer-level correction of induced label-noise memorization can alter generalization, with outcomes depending on the intervention and training noise.

record.problems: The principal results are often presented as plots without numerical values in the prose. The authors describe the ViT experiments as preliminary and note deviations and possible stitching-method limitations. Appendix A.4 cautions that only selected middle-block combinations were explored. One appendix result states r ≤ 8000, which is preserved as written.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying reported results were omitted. Figure-only accuracy curves are represented by the text's stated aggregate outcomes where available; individual plotted values are not reconstructed.

untested.parts: Fully random-label fitting versus natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe, including chance held-out accuracy under random-label training.
Width sweeps beyond the zero-training-error threshold and their test-error trajectories.
Convolutional versus fully connected training, local connectivity, and convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers and dependence on tuning or optimizer modifications.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects, training-set-size dependence, and removal with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Removal of examples selected by inclusion-based memorization scores versus random removal, followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to the supplied versions because every row links to none; this does not deny the reported stitching effects. Deliberately induced random-label memorization is the experimental setup, and is distinct from V8's inclusion-based memorization of naturally labeled examples. No omitted result in the supplied text warrants a verdict on V1–V8.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test fully random labels, held-out accuracy on randomly labeled examples, or the listed models and recipes.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold test.
Does not compare convolutional networks with fully connected networks trained from scratch.
Does not remove selected training examples and retrain.

rows.subject: noisy models across five architecture-dataset pairs
rows.operation_detail: Train on partially randomly relabeled data at stated noise ratios; evaluate accuracy on unseen clean test data.

conditions.value: custom CNN-SVHN; ResNet-18-CIFAR-10; ResNet-34-CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100; ResNet-50-CIFAR-100

rows.baseline: corresponding clean model; exact values not stated in text
rows.value: not stated; Figure 4 plots the values
rows.note: The prose says test accuracy improves with more clean layers stitched in, but does not state the unstitched noisy-model test accuracy numerically.
rows.check: Partially corrupted-label training and clean-test accuracy do not establish V1's fully random-label comparison. Exceeding 99% training accuracy is the stated stopping criterion; exact test baselines cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text.

rows.subject: clean-to-noisy stitched models across five architecture-dataset pairs
rows.operation_detail: Replace an initial noisy layer/block prefix with corresponding clean layers/blocks and train a stitching layer on validation data.
rows.baseline: noisy model; numerical baseline not stated
rows.value: roughly 8-10% test-performance boost after stitching the first clean layer/block for CNN-SVHN and ResNet-18-CIFAR-10
rows.note: The text gives this example for two model-dataset pairs; it describes a notable boost across all architectures.
rows.check: The 8–10% improvement concerns layer stitching, which no version names. The numerical example applies specifically to CNN-SVHN and ResNet-18-CIFAR-10; distinguish it from the qualitative cross-architecture finding.

rows.subject: clean-to-noisy stitched models across five architecture-dataset pairs
rows.operation_detail: Increase the clean prefix in the noisy model and train a stitching layer on validation data.

conditions.value: varied; exact values not stated for this result

rows.value: stitched-model test accuracy eventually matches clean-model performance at lcg; lcg is not the final layer
rows.note: The text states this trend across architectures and datasets; the exact accuracy values are plotted in Figure 4.
rows.check: Matching clean-model accuracy after stitching does not measure any supplied version.

rows.operation_detail: Replace an initial noisy layer/block prefix with corresponding clean layers/blocks and train a stitching layer on validation data.

rows.baseline: noisy model; exact values not stated in text
rows.value: near-random accuracy once the clean base reaches lcm
rows.note: The reported trend covers the tested architectures and datasets; plotted values are in Figure 2.

rows.subject: clean-to-noisy stitched models on SVHN and CIFAR-10
rows.operation_detail: Replace the first noisy layer/block with its clean counterpart.
rows.measure: accuracy on randomly labeled training inputs
rows.baseline: noisy model; exact values not stated in text
rows.value: below 50% after replacing only the first noisy layer/block
rows.note: This is described as a substantial reduction; near-random accuracy requires a critical clean prefix.
rows.check: Reduced recall of corrupted training labels after layer replacement does not measure any supplied version.

rows.subject: clean-to-noisy stitched models on CIFAR-100
rows.operation_detail: Replace an initial noisy block prefix with clean counterparts.
rows.measure: accuracy on randomly labeled training inputs
rows.baseline: noisy model; exact values not stated in text
rows.value: a drop similar to the stated below-50% example requires stitching clean layers at least up to the middle block
rows.note: The comparison is qualitative; exact accuracies are plotted in Figure 2.
rows.check: The required clean-prefix depth concerns stitching, rather than a supplied claim version.

rows.subject: noisy-to-clean stitched models across five architecture-dataset pairs
rows.operation_detail: Replace an initial clean layer/block prefix with corresponding noisy layers/blocks and train a stitching layer on validation data.
rows.measure: accuracy on randomly labeled training inputs
rows.baseline: random accuracy (100/N, N being the number of classes)
rows.value: close to random for shallow stitching depths
rows.note: Memorized accuracy begins to rise only after the noisy prefix passes a threshold.
rows.check: Near-chance corrupted-training-label accuracy in hybrid models is not evidence of absence of V1.

rows.subject: noisy-to-clean stitched models across five architecture-dataset pairs
rows.operation_detail: Increase the noisy prefix in the clean model while retaining a clean head.

conditions.value: all layers except output layer noisy

rows.measure: accuracy on randomly labeled training inputs
rows.baseline: random accuracy and fully noisy model; exact baselines not stated
rows.value: CNN-SVHN 20-30%; ResNet-34-CIFAR-10 at most 55%; ResNet-34-CIFAR-100 30%; ResNet-50-CIFAR-100 approximately 60%
rows.note: The text says noisy-to-clean stitched models never show full memorization. These examples are reported separately by model and dataset.
rows.check: Incomplete memorization after combining separately trained models does not qualify V1's capacity claim. Split the numerical examples by architecture and dataset; the prose gives four examples, not values for all five pairs.

rows.subject: noisy-to-clean stitched models across five architecture-dataset pairs
rows.operation_detail: Increase the noisy prefix in the clean model and train a stitching layer on validation data.

conditions.value: shallow prefix, then beyond critical depth lng

rows.baseline: clean model and fully noisy model; exact values not stated
rows.value: shallow noisy prefixes remain close to clean-model performance; beyond lng, accuracy declines toward the fully noisy model; even with all but the classifier noisy, accuracy is 15-20% higher than the noisy model at r = 50%
rows.note: The findings are described across architectures and noise levels; specific curves are plotted in Figure 5.
rows.check: The stitching-depth trajectory fits no version. The source describes improvements as large as 15–20% at 50% noise, rather than establishing that range for every architecture.

rows.subject: ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10
rows.stage_stated: trained on noisy variants, then one layer fine-tuned independently
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tune each layer independently on the validation dataset while freezing other layers.

conditions.value: multiple noisy variants; exact values not stated for this result

rows.value: fine-tuning the first block improves test accuracy; exact values are plotted in Figure 6
rows.note: The text says the increase is proportional to noise ratio r; exact numerical values are not stated.
rows.check: Single-block fine-tuning is outside the supplied versions. The baseline is the corresponding noisy model before fine-tuning.

rows.subject: ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10
rows.stage_stated: trained on noisy variants, then one layer fine-tuned independently
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tune each layer independently on the validation dataset while freezing other layers.
rows.measure: accuracy on randomly labeled training inputs
rows.note: The text states that retraining deeper layers predicts more memorized inputs correctly but does not exceed 80% accuracy.
rows.check: The accuracy is measured against true labels on previously corrupted training inputs, not against their assigned random labels. The 80% ceiling describes incomplete correction, not retained memorization accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10
rows.stage_stated: trained on noisy variants, then one layer fine-tuned independently
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tune one layer independently on memorized examples using their true labels.

conditions.value: randomly labeled training inputs with true labels
r ≤ 8000 for the stated degradation result

rows.value: degrades for all noise ratios r ≤ 8000; for large noise, improves after fine-tuning the first layer and with deeper fine-tuned layers, except the last residual block
rows.note: The source states r ≤ 8000; this value is preserved as written.
rows.check: The source's r ≤ 8000 is inconsistent with r being a percentage; the exact threshold is indeterminate. Retain only the qualitative small-noise degradation versus large-noise improvement unless corrected from another source. Baseline is the original noisy model.

rows.subject: ResNet-101 on CIFAR-100
rows.stage_stated: trained on noisy variants; stitched at representative locations
rows.operation_detail: Stitch clean prefixes into noisy models and noisy prefixes into clean models.
rows.measure: accuracy on randomly labeled training inputs
rows.value: a clean prefix through layer3.0 eliminates more than 50% memorization for large noise ratios; noisy-to-clean memorization emerges only when the noisy prefix reaches the last few residual blocks
rows.note: The experiment is described as preliminary; exact plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: The preliminary ResNet-101 stitching result fits no version. Split clean-to-noisy suppression and noisy-to-clean emergence into separate conditions.

rows.subject: ViT-Small on CIFAR-100
rows.stage_stated: trained on clean and noisy data; stitched after transformer blocks
rows.operation_detail: Stitch clean and noisy model prefixes in both directions; train stitching layer on validation data.
rows.baseline: clean model; exact values not stated
rows.value: matches clean-model test accuracy after stitching clean layers through blocks.6
rows.note: Prose states the result for both noise ratios.
rows.check: Recovery of clean-model accuracy by stitching ViT blocks does not measure any supplied version.

rows.subject: ViT-Small on CIFAR-100
rows.stage_stated: trained on clean and noisy data; stitched after transformer blocks
rows.operation_detail: Stitch clean and noisy model prefixes in both directions; train stitching layer on validation data.
rows.measure: accuracy on randomly labeled training inputs
rows.value: a sudden, small spike in memorized accuracy
rows.note: The source gives no exact value for the spike.
rows.check: The local spike fits no version. The source is internally inconsistent: the initial observation identifies blocks.3, whereas the later discussion identifies blocks.2.

rows.subject: ViT-Small on CIFAR-100
rows.stage_stated: trained on clean and noisy data; stitched after transformer blocks
rows.operation_detail: Stitch noisy prefixes into the clean model and evaluate.
rows.baseline: noisy counterpart; exact values not stated
rows.value: always significantly better than the noisy counterpart; at r = 25% the decline is gradual, while at r = 50% it is sharp
rows.note: The source reports different trajectories by noise ratio.
rows.check: ViT stitching trajectories do not measure any supplied version; separate the 25% and 50% noise conditions.

rows.subject: ViT-Small on CIFAR-100
rows.stage_stated: trained on clean and noisy data; stitched after transformer blocks
rows.operation_detail: Stitch noisy prefixes into the clean model and evaluate memorized accuracy.
rows.measure: accuracy on randomly labeled training inputs
rows.baseline: random accuracy; exact value not stated
rows.value: memorization emerges only after a significant number of noisy blocks are stitched; never reaches full memorization even when all but the output layer are noisy
rows.note: The text reports a qualitative result without exact accuracies.
rows.check: Incomplete memorization by a stitched ViT is outside V1's ordinary-training comparison.

rows.subject: ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10
rows.stage_stated: trained on noisy variants; middle blocks replaced with clean counterparts
rows.operation_detail: Insert one clean middle block or consecutive subsets of clean middle blocks into the noisy model using two stitching layers.

conditions.value: single middle block; subsets layer1.1 through layer2.1 and layer3.0 through layer4.2

rows.measure: accuracy on randomly labeled training inputs
rows.baseline: noisy model; exact values not stated
rows.value: clean middle-block insertions reduce memorized accuracy; larger consecutive subsets reduce it further
rows.note: Exact values are plotted in Figure 9 and not stated in the prose.
rows.check: Middle-block replacement fits no version. Block names are inconsistent within the source: Figure 9 labels multiple-block boundaries layer1.0 to layer2.1 and layer2.1 to layer4.0, while the prose includes layer4.2, which is not a ResNet-18 block. Flag the exact insertion condition as unresolved.

rows.subject: ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10
rows.stage_stated: trained on noisy variants; middle blocks replaced with clean counterparts
rows.operation_detail: Insert one clean middle block or consecutive subsets of clean middle blocks into the noisy model using two stitching layers.

conditions.value: single middle block; subsets layer1.1 through layer2.1 and layer3.0 through layer4.2

rows.baseline: clean model; exact values not stated
rows.value: none of the explored insertions matches clean-model test accuracy at any noise ratio
rows.note: The authors caution that a comprehensive evaluation would require exploring more block combinations.
rows.check: Failure of selected middle-block insertions to recover clean-model accuracy fits no version. The insertion conditions inherit the source's inconsistent block names noted for R18.
